title: Throttle-aware batching fix to resolve cross-tenant long-tail latency escalations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Customer escalation from a large enterprise (FinCo Europe) reported sustained tail latency spikes for multi-turn long-context chat sessions. Root symptoms: long-context sessions intermittently blocked shorter, latency-sensitive requests across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The problem manifests as 95th-99th percentile token latencies spiking from ~60ms to 900-1200ms for short requests during sustained long-context generation bursts. The stacktrace and tracing indicate a combination of admission-window starvation + aggressive KV cache eviction churn when preemption events occur. This ticket tracks investigation, temporary mitigations, and the proposed throttle-aware batching fix to avoid cross-tenant starvation and reduce long-context tail amplification.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a dedicated pool with mixed tenant workload (tenant A: sustained long-context streaming generation >= 8k tokens; tenant B: frequent short-response requests ~1-6 tokens).
Send parallel bursts: Tenant A creates 10 concurrent long streaming sessions; Tenant B sends 40 short requests per second for 2 minutes.
Observe cluster-level token latency: short requests P95/P99 increase, KV cache eviction rate spikes in the same window.
Reproduce in Hosted by routing two test API keys to the same region with workload mix above; observe similar tail degradation intermittently.

03-03-2026: Heap of logs indicate preemptive dequeue calls triggered by tenant fairness policy causing eviction of long-context KV entries and immediate re-population, thrashing memory and stalling scheduler cycles.
03-04-2026: Reproduced locally in dedicated-sim environment. Created deterministic replay test case: repo PR for test harness https://github.com/redwood-inference/replay-tests/pull/412
03-05-2026: Desktop session with Customer Success + FinCo engineer; they provided exact request shape and rate limiting profile which accelerated repro.
root_cause: Scheduler admission is too agnostic to active KV cache heat. Preemptive fairness code preempted long-context batches without accounting for cost of KV eviction and refill. This causes repeated eviction/regeneration cycles on hot KV entries, increasing scheduler CPU and blocking short-request admission windows, amplifying the long-context tail latency across tenants.
mitigations: Hotfix A (deployed 03-06-2026 to affected Dedicated pools): Temporarily reduce preemption frequency and extend grace window for in-flight long-context batches. Immediate P99 drop ~60% in customer repro cluster.
Hotfix B (deployed 03-07-2026 to Hosted fallback layer): Add KV eviction guard to avoid evicting entries referenced by active session tokens for 500ms post-preemption.
Customer workaround: Route FinCo high-throughput long-context sessions to dedicated reserved pools with isolation until fix is fully rolled out.
proposed_fix: Implement 'throttle-aware batching' in the admission controller. Key components: (1) admission weighting that factors estimated KV refills cost and active-session cache heat, (2) a soft-throttle token bucket for long-context generators to smooth ingress rather than abrupt preemption, and (3) an eviction-safety window to avoid immediate eviction of recently-accessed KV segments. This reduces repeated eviction/regeneration cycles and lowers scheduler churn. Implementation details in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892
rollout_plan: Canary build runtime-2.3.1+patch on 3 Dedicated staging clusters (control/variant) for 48 hours with synthetic mixed workload harness.
If metrics pass (P95 short-request latency improvement >= 40% and KV eviction rate decrease >= 50%), promote to 10% of Hosted traffic and one additional Private customer cluster.
Gradual ramp to 100% over 72 hours with automatic rollback triggers on regression thresholds for error rate or tail latency.
Post-rollout runbook added to on-call playbook and FinCo support thread notified of expected timeline.
test_plan: Add deterministic replay test for long-context + burst short-request mix to nightly e2e suite: replay-tests PR #412.
Unit tests for admission weighting calculations and throttle token bucket edge cases.
Chaos test: force KV eviction thrash to verify eviction-safety window prevents repeat churn and does not leak memory.
Load test with simulated multi-tenant traffic at 2x received rates for 6 hours in staging.
monitoring_and_alerts: New Grafana panel: 'Admission weight vs KV refill rate' with alert if KV refills per second > 100 and short-request P99 > 500ms for 5m.
Add burn-in SLO guard: if dedicated pool shows tail latency regression after rollout, automatic traffic shift to fallback model variant (lower KV footprint).
On-call alert added: ENG-runtime-pager if cross-tenant short-request P95 rises > 200ms from baseline for more than 3 minutes.
